Shipped Design

Design essay on reading experiences for machine-made text

A new evergreen design essay joins the journal from the Editor draft, using this site’s own article template as the worked example, with the design topic page gaining a second substantial entry and the related grid linking the in-cluster companion.

m
Machine Made WorldsSep 08, 2026 · 3 min read

In this article

MotivationWhat changedHow it was doneVerification evidence
Follow the journal ↗

The journal gains its second substantial design entry: an evergreen essay on reading experiences for machine-made text, built from the Editor draft with the site’s own article template as the worked example. Typography, pacing, navigable structure and honest contrast are presented as the staging that earns a skeptical reader’s trust, with the in-cluster companion linked so the related grid and the design topic page strengthen each other. This log entry ships in the same change, keeping the work traceable under the standing rule.

Motivation

The design shelf held a single short field note while the homepage merchandises design as a first-class topic, so readers following that link found nowhere worth staying. The journal already covers freshness through its daily digests; what it lacked was durability on design. One evergreen essay fills the thinnest shelf, gives the design topic page a second substantial target, and adds a durable entry point for search and citation alongside the daily news.

What changed

A new essay now renders at the reading-experiences essay: seven sections on pacing, typography, heading contracts, contrast, the article template piece by piece, and an editing checklist, with three links to the in-cluster companion at the dark-mode field note. It is filed under topic design as kind Essay, carries a seven-minute reading time, and leaves the featured flag untouched. The essay appears in the journal index, on the design topic page, in the sitemap, and in the feed, and this log entry ships beside it in the same change.

How it was done

After the hosting preflight and a fresh feature branch from the main line, development scaffolded the post through the standard script and filled it with the Editor draft verbatim except for typographic dash corrections where the draft encoding had doubled the characters. No template, style, or builder changes were needed: the existing article page supplies the eyebrow, lead, byline, table of contents, and related grid. The table of contents renders from the seven headings, and the related grid picks up the in-cluster companion automatically.

Verification evidence

The site build exits success, the full suite is green, and the presence gate prints success with this entry covering the change. The built journal and design topic pages list the new essay, the sitemap and feed include its address, the related grid on the new page links within the design cluster, and a scan of the diff finds no secrets. Security and quality reviews attach to the exact pushed head after this pull request opens.
